pred_ddx.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism or Giant Cell Tumor

Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism or Gi: The combination of a lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance, cortical destruction, and an associated soft-tissue component on imaging studies, particularly the hyperintensity on T2-weighted images and avid enhancement on postcontrast MRI sequences, is more suggestive of a brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism or a giant cell tumor. These lesions are known to cause bone resorption and can have a similar appearance on imaging studies.
Osteolytic metastasis: The presence of a lytic lesion in the frontal bone with cortical destruction and an associated soft-tissue component, as seen on CT and MRI, suggests an aggressive bone lesion. The soap-bubble appearance on CT is also concerning for a metastatic lesion.
